messages:
Alex: Quick RFC follow-up: I'm proposing a hybrid enforcement model for abuse control. Key questions: where should enforcement live (edge-only, central-only, or hybrid), how do we sync grace credits across regions, and what telemetry do we need for blame and billing?
Maria: high-level sketch pls. I want to see a common happy-path and an outage path.
Alex: Happy-path: request hits edge -> edge applies local grace (fast, no RPC) -> if local exhausted, edge consults central soft-budget via a small delta RPC -> if central allows, edge proceeds and deducts local delta; otherwise central returns penalty token.
Jamal: Concern: any RPC on the request path risks p99 blowups. Can we make central consult async-ish? e.g., edge makes provisional admit then central reconciles and can retro-penalize?
Sasha: Yes. Make edge authoritative for immediate decisions. Central issues adjustments (positive/negative deltas) later. But central should be able to issue immediate short-term penalties for flagged abuse (via a push stream or push token cache).
Ethan: Implementation idea: two control planes: (1) Pullable compact soft-budget state (rebalance every 5-15s) and (2) push penalty events for urgent blocks. Edge uses soft-budget locally, and listens for push penalties.
Maria: How to prevent region hotspots getting unfair share? If credits are region-local, a tenant with traffic in one region can consume more.
Alex: Options: region-local buckets with periodic global rebalance, or global logical quota with probabilistic sampling at edges (sample some requests and ask central). Hybrid approach again: local buckets + a global bank that can be drained if a tenant exceeds global allowance.
Jamal: That global bank could become a choke point. Add circuit-breakers: if central latency > X ms or error rate > Y, edges flip to conservative mode (reduce local buckets by factor).
Sasha: Data model: store credits as int64 counters per tenant+edge with monotonic delta writes. Use delta-only API: POST {tenant, delta, idempotency_key}. Central only keeps aggregates and returns horizon/token if needed. Keep per-request payload tiny.
Ethan: For streaming/generation, preauth vs actual usage: preauth for max tokens, then on completion send reconcile delta = actual - preauth (negative if under). Must be idempotent and deduped by request_id.
Maria: ops playbook: if central unreachable for >30s -> edges halve preauth budgets and refuse large preauths (>X tokens). Notify SRE and trigger runbook. Document customer-visible errors: higher 429s but no silent overcharge.
Alex: Telemetry proposal: emit a single request-level event: {trace_id, req_id, tenant, edge, decision: ALLOW|DENY|THROTTLE, local_grace_before, local_grace_after, central_sync: OK|TIMEOUT, penalty_source}. Also metrics: gauge(local_grace_remaining{tenant,edge}), hist(central_rpc_ms).
Sasha: Also emit reconciliation events: {req_id, preauth, actual, delta_written, idempotency_key, reconcile_status}. Helps debug refunds.
Jamal: Testing: we need synthetic traffic tests that simulate central slowdowns, and surge tests that try to borrow global bank. Plan chaos experiments with cut-off central and verify edges enter conservative mode.
Ethan: SDK changes: add idempotency_key generation and attach to preauth/reconcile calls. Make client retry safe and surface central_timeouts distinctly so callers can instrument.
ops-bot: perf-tests/credit-delta-run: 8/10 passing. Failures show transient 504s to central when load spiked.
Maria: We should quantify latency impact: measure happy-path edge-only: add ~0.2ms; edge+central sync (sync path): +20-40ms p50, +100-200ms p99 depending on region. Put those numbers in RFC and call out SLOs.
Alex: Action items: 1) add hybrid architecture diagram + control-plane push/pull behavior, 2) define delta API shape and idempotency contract, 3) write ops playbook for central outage, 4) add telemetry schema and example dashboards, 5) implement preauth/reconcile prototype in edge proxy.
Maria: assigning: Jamal -> chaos tests, Sasha -> telemetry schema + dashboard, Ethan -> SDK idempotency + client retries, Alex -> prototype + RFC update.
Jamal: I'll queue chaos tests once prototype branch is up.
Sasha: Quick note: ensure reconciliation supports partial refunds and negative deltas. Also consider batching reconcile writes to central for efficiency.
Ethan: I'll make the SDK batch small reconcilations and attach request-level trace ids.
Alex: Good work. I'll update the RFC and include sample metrics + expected customer behavior. Will follow up with PR for the edge prototype.
Maria: Thanks.
ops-bot: ci/edge-proxy-preauth job: flaky. see logs: `rpc to central-credit failed: deadline exceeded`
Alex: we'll add retries with backoff and failfast to conservative mode. End.
